headline: Nearly 100 Electric School Buses Coming to New York City
meta_description: New York City is deploying nearly 100 electric school buses to reduce emissions and cut transportation costs for students.
summary_short: New York City is rolling out nearly 100 electric school buses, delivering cleaner air and lower costs for students while strengthening the city's power grid.
body:
New York City is deploying nearly 100 electric school buses, marking a major shift toward sustainable student transportation and grid-friendly infrastructure.

The fleet represents part of a broader transition already underway: more than 8,500 electric school buses are operating across the country. By switching to electric power, NYC schools will reduce diesel emissions that affect neighborhoods near bus routes while lowering fuel and maintenance costs—savings that can be redirected toward education.

Beyond cleaner commutes, these buses offer an unexpected benefit. When parked and connected to the grid during off-peak hours, they can store and supply power back to the city's electrical system. This vehicle-to-grid capability transforms school buses from one-way consumers of energy into active participants in urban infrastructure, helping stabilize power during high-demand periods while the buses sit idle.
quick_facts: Nearly 100 electric school buses deploying to New York City streets
More than 8,500 electric school buses already operating nationwide
Buses can feed power back to NYC's electrical grid when parked
